slides.title: Week 13 Completion — Finishing the Mission Week

items.text: “Before we walk forward, we finish the Mission week” — unfinished downhill answers finish here
Two weeks of living with the question usually deepens it — one sentence, now, to the room
A parent opens the round; teens choose their own depth after — pass-anytime holds
The answers carry forward to the Week 21 commissioning
Practice check: one small action aligned with your downhill mission — ninety seconds, one sentence on what happened
The condition is not “if we feel it.” It is “if we do not give up” — Paul assumes the weariness
The reaping is tied to the season, and the season is God's — our part is the not-giving-up
Nobody white-knuckles their way through years; people with a rhythm walk through years
The break is coming — what carries the practices across a gap is not momentum; it is a rhythm you built on purpose
So we build it tonight, before the gap, not after it

panel.label: GALATIANS 6:9 (ESV)
lines: “And let us not grow weary of doing good, for in due season we will reap, if we do not give up.”

items.text: The whole series folded into one page — you have already received every practice on this card
Daily — the morning question, the evening journal note, PROAPT if the season allows
Weekly — one specific person who knows what you are working on, and a sabbath rhythm
Monthly — a clearing time and a Four-Connects review. Seasonally — the deeper work
One rule for the build: “write the rhythm you will actually keep, not the one that impresses you”
The starter plan begins with two practices totaling six minutes a day — six honest minutes is a real rhythm
Twenty minutes in family clusters — in your own handwriting, on the build sheet
Specific beats vague — “morning question, 6:50, kitchen table, before my phone” is a rhythm
The weekly partner line is the most important line on the sheet — name an actual person
Build down, not up — which two practices survive exam season? Start there; the card lets you add later
Close: each participant reads their daily line aloud to the cluster — a parent first; pass-anytime holds
Parents, this next part is for you — nobody answers tonight. This week, at home, for the willing: unhurried, no audience, phone away, yours first
What has it been like to live with me all these years?
What have been my messages to you?
How have I wounded you?
What would you like from me going forward?
The guards — willing only, both directions; receive without defending (listening questions and “thank you” only); invisible by default; a letter counts; the Section 6 boundary

panel.label: PSALM 139:23–24
lines: Asked of God, it is worship. Asked of your family, it is the bravest form of the same prayer.
James 1:19 — quick to hear, slow to speak.

slides.title: Between-Session Practice — This Week and Across the Break

items.text: The Four Questions (for the willing) — the parent asks their teen at home; married parents also ask their spouse, separately. “Not yet” is a full answer for everyone
Run the Rhythm Card as built — for real, at the times and places written on it; the break is its first field test
Journal the holds and the slips — one line a day; no fixing, no guilt-engine. The slips are data, not verdicts
The returning rule — miss a day: begin again on the next available day. Do not start over; do not double up. Returning is the goal
The morning question and evening note continue inside the rhythm — the practices have stopped being assignments and become a life
